memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the day of firstfruits, when you present to the LORD an offering of new grain during the Festival of Weeks, hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old as an aroma pleasing to the LORD. - Num 28:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Festival of Weeks, or the day of firstfruits, celebrated the first portion of the harvest offered back to God. Before enjoying the full harvest, Israel presented the first and best to the Lord, acknowledging that all their provision came from His hand. It was a festival of gratitude and trust.

Offering the firstfruits was an act of faith. By giving God the first of the harvest, the people declared that they trusted Him to provide the rest. They put God first, not last, in their gratitude. This guarded their hearts against the pride of thinking their harvest was purely the work of their own hands.

There is a rich principle here about honouring God with our first and best. Whatever God has given us, whether time, resources, or ability, we honour Him by offering the first portion back to Him rather than the leftovers. Gratitude that puts God first shapes a heart that trusts His provision.

Wonderfully, Scripture calls Christ the firstfruits of those who have died, the first to rise, guaranteeing the resurrection of all who belong to Him (1 Cor 15:20). His resurrection is the firstfruits of the great harvest to come. As we honour God with our firstfruits, we do so trusting the risen Christ, in whom our future is secure. Give God your first and best, resting in His faithful provision.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give God your first and best, or only your leftovers?
2. How does offering firstfruits express trust in God's provision?
3. What does it mean that Christ is the firstfruits of the resurrection?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to honour You with my first and best, trusting Your faithful provision. Thank You that Christ is the firstfruits of the resurrection, in whom my future is forever secure. Amen.
